div.h1: 蟹 逅 伦 敦！
div.div: 跟着帕丁顿熊和电影地图游伦敦：从落地第一顿炸鱼薯条，到诺丁山书店、裁缝街 Kingsman，涉及旅行打卡、点餐、天气吐槽、电影取景地介绍等真实旅行场景的英文表达。

div.span: S1 开场：帕丁顿熊的比喻｜Opening: The Paddington Metaphor
S2 初到伦敦：大本钟与天气｜First Impressions: Big Ben & Weather
S3 新冠纪念墙｜COVID Memorial Wall
S4 落地第一顿：炸鱼薯条 & 中餐｜First Meal: Fish & Chips & Chinese
S5 酒吧景观位｜Bar with a View
S6 自然历史博物馆｜Natural History Museum
S7 诺丁山 & 电影书店｜Notting Hill & the Bookshop
S8 裁缝街 & Kingsman｜Savile Row & Kingsman
S9 最后一天：晴天伦敦｜Final Day: Sunny London

div.h2: S1 开场：帕丁顿熊的比喻｜Opening: The Paddington Metaphor 00:00–00:51

div.p: 情景：博主在伦敦开场，用帕丁顿熊的故事比喻自己远道而来的心情——从遥远的地方坐飞机过来，带着一箱设备而非果酱。

tr.td: 伦敦有一只非常著名的小熊，就是帕丁顿熊。
There's a very famous little bear in London — Paddington Bear.
他是从很远的秘鲁坐船过来的。
He came all the way from Peru by boat.
我觉得我跟他特别的像，也是从大老远的地方坐飞机过来的。
I feel like I'm a lot like him — I also came from far away, but by plane.
但我大概不是果酱，带的是一箱子的设备。
But instead of marmalade, I brought a suitcase full of gear.
帕丁顿来到伦敦时，脖子上挂着一张写着「请照顾好这只熊」的纸条。
When Paddington arrived in London, he had a tag around his neck that said "Please look after this bear."
第一次来到伦敦的我也想借用一下这句话：请照顾好这只蟹。
As a first-timer in London, I'd like to borrow that line: Please look after this crab.
在真正站在这里之前，我对伦敦的认识其实还蛮零碎的。
Before actually standing here, my knowledge of London was pretty scattered.
大本钟、阴晴不定的天气，还有电影里那些似曾相识的街道。
Big Ben, unpredictable weather, and streets that felt familiar from movies.
所以这一次我想认真当一回游客，也想看看那些电影里的地方现实中到底是什么样的。
So this time I want to be a proper tourist and see what those movie locations actually look like in real life.
欢迎收看本期的邂逅时间——伦敦。
Welcome to this episode of Encounter Time — London.

ul.li: I'm a lot like him → I really identify with him / I can totally relate to him
all the way from... → all the way over from... / from as far away as...
pretty scattered → all over the place / kind of random / a bit of a mixed bag
a proper tourist → a real tourist / do the whole tourist thing / play tourist for real
借用了这句话 → I'd like to steal that line / I'm gonna borrow that phrase / let me quote that

div.div: Chunks：all the way from… / a lot like… / instead of… / pretty (scattered) / borrow that line / look after

div.h2: S2 初到伦敦：大本钟与天气｜First Impressions: Big Ben & Weather 00:55–01:20

div.p: 情景：博主落地伦敦，站在大本钟前吐槽伦敦的阴雨天气，顺便科普伦敦年降雨量其实不如上海。

tr.td: 家人們到伦敦了！
Hey guys, we've made it to London!
既然是第一次来，那有些游客作业总还是要交一下的。后面是大本钟。
Since it's my first time, I've gotta do the obligatory tourist stuff. Big Ben's right behind me.
但今天一到伦敦这个天气就非常典型，特别的伦敦——阴雨绵绵的。
But the weather today is just so typical, so London — drizzly and grey.
但是据说其实伦敦全年的降雨量它没有上海多，这个你改心。
But apparently London's annual rainfall is actually less than Shanghai's — let that sink in.
主要是它每次都是下一点点毛毛雨。可能这就是为什么经常看到伦敦人下雨天不打伞的原因吧。
It's mainly because it's always just a light drizzle. Maybe that's why you often see Londoners not bothering with umbrellas.

ul.li: we've made it! → we're here! / we've arrived! / touchdown London!
obligatory tourist stuff → the must-do tourist checklist / the standard tourist routine
so typical, so London → classic London / peak London / couldn't be more London
let that sink in → think about that for a second / chew on that / wrap your head around that
not bothering with umbrellas → can't be bothered with umbrellas / don't even bother with umbrellas

div.div: Chunks：we've made it / gotta do the... / right behind me / so typical / let that sink in / not bothering with…

div.h2: S3 新冠纪念墙｜COVID Memorial Wall 01:21–01:44

div.p: 情景：博主路过一面满是爱心的墙，发现每颗爱心代表一位新冠逝者。语气从轻松转为沉重。

tr.td: 我后面这个墙上全都是爱心。
The wall behind me is covered in hearts.
但这里每颗爱心都代表一位新冠逝者。
But each heart here represents someone who passed away from COVID.

ul.li: is covered in hearts → is full of hearts / is plastered with hearts / has hearts all over it
passed away from COVID → died of COVID / lost their life to COVID / was a COVID victim
represents → stands for / symbolizes / is a tribute to

div.div: Chunks：covered in… / each… represents… / passed away from… / in memory of…

div.h2: S4 落地第一顿：炸鱼薯条 & 中餐｜First Meal: Fish & Chips & Chinese 01:44–02:36

div.p: 情景：博主在伦敦的第一顿吃了炸鱼薯条（仪式感），但还是跑去吃了中餐的肉夹馍（中国胃），感叹中餐出了国价格涨了但魅力不减。

tr.td: 落地伦敦的第一顿当然要吃炸鱼薯条了。
For my first meal in London, fish and chips was a no-brainer.
我们找到一家从1988年开到现在、号称英国顶尖的老店。
We found a place that's been around since 1988, supposedly one of the best in the UK.
还碰到一个当地人跟我们说这是伦敦最好吃的炸鱼薯条。
Even ran into a local who told us it's the best fish and chips in London.
最好吃不敢说，但伦敦第一顿的仪式感算是有了。
Can't say if it's the best, but at least we got that first-meal-in-London ritual out of the way.
仪式归仪式，但中国胃是不一样的。所以我们来了一家从某个年代开到现在的老店。
Rituals aside, a Chinese stomach is a different story. So we came to this long-standing spot.
来看看这个西安的肉夹馍，折算下来一百多块钱一份。
Check out this Xi'an-style roujiamo — works out to over a hundred yuan each.
中餐出了国，价格是涨了，魅力倒是一点没打折。
Chinese food abroad — the price goes up, but the appeal doesn't drop one bit.

ul.li: a no-brainer → an obvious choice / a given / goes without saying
been around since 1988 → been open since 1988 / has been serving since 1988
ran into a local → bumped into a local / a local came up to us
got that ritual out of the way → checked that box / ticked that off the list
rituals aside → that said / having said that / but let's be real
a different story → a whole other matter / that's another thing entirely
works out to → comes to / adds up to / that's about
the appeal doesn't drop one bit → still just as good / every bit as tempting

div.div: Chunks：a no-brainer / been around since… / ran into… / got… out of the way / …aside / a different story / works out to… / doesn't drop one bit

div.h2: S5 酒吧景观位｜Bar with a View 02:36–02:56

div.p: 情景：博主没有预约就去了伦敦一家有名的酒吧，结果意外坐到了全场景观位——体验感拉满，账单也一样。

tr.td: 伦敦还有一家挺有名的酒吧，但是我没有预约，最后只能坐在了吧台位。
There's this pretty famous bar in London, but I didn't have a reservation, so I ended up at the counter.
但是没有想到这个临时的座位真的是全场景佳的景观位。
But who would've thought — this last-minute seat turned out to be the best view in the whole place.
怎么样，体验感拉满吧？不过账单也一样。
Pretty amazing experience, right? Though the bill was just as impressive.

ul.li: ended up at the counter → wound up at the bar / had to settle for the bar seat
who would've thought → turns out / surprisingly enough / as it happens
turned out to be → ended up being / happened to be / was actually
体验感拉满 → a top-tier experience / the experience was off the charts / couldn't have asked for more
the bill was just as impressive → the bill matched the view / you pay for what you get / the price tag was equally stunning

div.div: Chunks：ended up at… / who would've thought / turned out to be / off the charts / just as impressive

div.h2: S6 自然历史博物馆｜Natural History Museum 02:58–04:23

div.p: 情景：博主拿电影当旅行地图，来到帕丁顿熊差点被做成标本的地方——自然历史博物馆，看恐龙化石和动物标本。

tr.td: 虽然伦敦是第一次来，但有些画面早就在电影里面见过了。
Even though it's my first time in London, some of these scenes I've already seen in movies.
比如眼前的这个帕丁顿车站，是不是还挺熟悉的？
Like Paddington Station right here — does it look familiar?
今天我们就拿电影当地图，看看银幕外的伦敦。
Today we're using movies as our map to see London beyond the screen.
跟随着帕丁顿熊的足迹，我来到了英国的自然历史博物馆，这里就是帕丁顿熊差点被抓起做成标本的地方。
Following Paddington's footsteps, I ended up at the Natural History Museum — the very place where Paddington was almost turned into a stuffed specimen.
哇这里真的好壮观！挑高非常的高，像一个城堡一样。
Wow, this place is absolutely stunning! The ceiling is so high, it's like a castle.
这个大厅里面最值得看的就是这个被吊起来的蓝鲸化石。
The main thing to see in this hall is the blue whale skeleton hanging from the ceiling.
它整个动作就是一个向下俯冲捕食的动作，我感觉站在它下面特别的小。
It's posed mid-dive, like it's swooping down to catch prey. I feel so tiny standing underneath it.
这些化石看着确实挺震撼的，但这里还有很多动物标本。
The fossils are genuinely impressive, but there are also loads of animal specimens here.
真的每一只都栩栩如生。能近距离看到这么多难得一见的标本，确实挺厉害的。
Every single one looks so lifelike. Getting to see so many rare specimens up close is pretty amazing.
只是关于它们生前的故事咱就不了解了。希望它们都是在生命结束以后才以这种方式被留在这里的。
Though I don't really know the stories of how they lived. I just hope they ended up here after their lives ran their natural course.

ul.li: beyond the screen → off-screen / in real life / the real thing
following someone's footsteps → retracing someone's steps / walking in someone's path
absolutely stunning → breathtaking / jaw-dropping / out of this world
mid-dive → in mid-lunge / frozen mid-pounce / caught in the act of diving
swooping down → diving down / plunging / lunging
feel so tiny → feel so small / feel dwarfed / feel puny
lifelike → so realistic / true to life / uncannily real
up close → in person / face to face / right in front of you

div.div: Chunks：beyond the screen / following… footsteps / the very place where… / posed mid-dive / feel so tiny / up close / ran their natural course

div.h2: S7 诺丁山 & 电影书店｜Notting Hill & the Bookshop 04:27–05:10

div.p: 情景：博主来到诺丁山，探寻电影《诺丁山》中男女主角相遇的书店原址，发现电影和现实的差距——书店其实是纪念品店，真正的灵感来自另一家从未拍过电影的书店。

tr.td: 不知道有多少人是先看了《诺丁山》，后来才知道伦敦真的有这个地方叫诺丁山。
I wonder how many people watched Notting Hill first and only later found out it's an actual place in London.
电影里那间小小的旅行书店，也成了很多人记住这里的原因。
That tiny travel bookshop in the movie is what made this place stick in so many people's minds.
这就是电影中男女主角相遇的142号店，但实际上它并不是一家书店，而是一个纪念品商店。
This is number 142, where the leads meet in the film — but it's not actually a bookshop, it's a souvenir store.
实际上电影中书店的灵感是来自于有生活的这家书店，但有意思的是这里其实也没有真的拍过电影。
The real-life inspiration for the bookshop was actually this other bookstore, but funnily enough, they never filmed there either.
剧组只是照着当时的书店在摄影棚里重新搭了一间。
The crew just built a replica of it on a soundstage.
你看电影不一定是真的，但它确实能让一条街变成让全世界人都来打卡的地方——这个倒是真的。
Movies may not be real, but they can definitely turn a street into a place people from all over the world come to check out — that part is very real.

ul.li: only later found out → it wasn't until later that I realized / only discovered afterwards
stick in someone's mind → make an impression / leave a mark / be etched in memory
funnily enough → ironically / the funny thing is / here's the twist
built a replica → recreated it / made a copy / reconstructed it
on a soundstage → on a studio set / on a film lot / indoors at a studio
come to check out → flock to see / make a pilgrimage to / travel to visit

div.div: Chunks：only later found out / stick in someone's mind / funnily enough / built a replica / on a soundstage / come to check out / that part is very real

div.h2: S8 裁缝街 & Kingsman｜Savile Row & Kingsman 05:20–06:41

div.p: 情景：博主来到伦敦裁缝街 Savile Row，探访 Kingsman 电影灵感来源的百年西装店，偷拍店内却被默许，发现一件普通西装要两千多英镑。

tr.td: 这里就是伦敦的裁缝街，有的店铺已经开了几百年了。
This is Savile Row — some of these shops have been around for centuries.
听说这边一套定制西装要几千英镑，要等六个星期。
I heard a bespoke suit here costs a few thousand pounds and takes six weeks.
不过让这条街出圈的不只是西装，而是一部叫 Kingsman 的电影。
But what really put this street on the map wasn't just the suits — it was a movie called Kingsman.
你看这写的 Kingsman。这家店是1849年的时候开的。
See, it says Kingsman right here. This shop first opened in 1849.
据说当时《王牌特工》的导演就是在这里量体彩衣的时候突然来了灵感，于是就拍了这部电影。
Apparently the director of Kingsman was here getting fitted when inspiration struck, and that's how the movie was born.
来，看看这件西装的价钱。好贵，两万多。
Let's take a look at the price of this suit. So expensive — over twenty thousand.
走进去之后才发现它们上面写了不让我们拍摄，但我还是偷偷摸摸拍了一点。
After walking in, I noticed a sign saying no filming — but I still snuck in a few shots.
好像也没有制止我，整个偷感非常重。
They didn't seem to stop me either, so the whole thing felt super sneaky.
我悄悄看了一下，它里面的衣服价格还蛮高的，要两千多磅一件。
I took a quiet look — the prices inside are pretty steep, over two thousand pounds a piece.
就是普通黑色的西装，可能只是我看不出它的特别之处。
It was just a plain black suit — maybe I just can't tell what makes it special.
不过这地方特别有名，像很多英国的政要，比如丘吉尔、威廉王子，都在这边定制过西装。
But this place is seriously famous — loads of British figures like Churchill and Prince William have had suits made here.

ul.li: been around for centuries → been standing for hundreds of years / have centuries of history
put this street on the map → made this street famous / put this street in the spotlight
getting fitted → being measured / having a fitting / trying on suits
inspiration struck → he got the idea / a lightbulb went off / it hit him
snuck in a few shots → secretly filmed a bit / got some sneaky footage / stole a few clips
super sneaky → so furtive / very stealth-mode / total sneak vibes
pretty steep → pretty pricey / on the expensive side / not cheap at all
can't tell what makes it special → don't see what the fuss is about / can't spot the difference

div.div: Chunks：put… on the map / getting fitted / inspiration struck / snuck in a few shots / super sneaky / pretty steep / can't tell what makes it special

div.h2: S9 最后一天：晴天的伦敦｜Final Day: Sunny London 06:44–07:19

div.p: 情景：博主在伦敦的最后一天终于放晴了，阳光下的伦敦像换了一座城市。临别感言——电影里的地方找到了，电影之外的伦敦可能还得再来几次。

tr.td: 在伦敦的这几天，雨就没怎么停过，但到了最后一天——哎，天晴了。
The rain barely let up during my days in London, but on the final day — hey, the sun came out.
大本钟还是那个大本钟，可太阳一出来，看起来就像换了一座城市。
Big Ben is still Big Ben, but when the sun comes out, it feels like a whole different city.
至于伦敦到底是什么样，我第一次来确实说不太清。
As for what London is really like — honestly, I can't quite put my finger on it after just one visit.
电影里的那些地方算是找到了，但电影之外的伦敦可能还得再来几次。
I managed to find all those movie locations, but the London beyond the movies? Might take a few more trips.
当然也欢迎屏幕前的你来分享一下，你眼中的伦敦是什么样子。
And of course, I'd love for you guys to share — what does London look like through your eyes?

ul.li: barely let up → hardly stopped / almost never let up / was pretty much nonstop
the sun came out → it cleared up / the sun finally showed up / it brightened up
feels like a whole different city → looks like a completely different place / it's like night and day
can't quite put my finger on it → can't really pin it down / hard to sum up / I'm not quite sure how to describe it
I managed to find → I was able to track down / I did get to see / I checked off
might take a few more trips → might need a few more visits / probably deserves another go / I'll have to come back for that

div.div: Chunks：barely let up / the sun came out / a whole different city / put my finger on it / managed to find / might take a few more / through your eyes

div.h2: 今日可练 & 认知转变

ol.li: 「我从大老远的中国飞过来的。」→ I came all the way from China.
「这家店1988年就开了。」→ This place has been around since 1988.
「我就随便坐了吧台，结果竟然是最佳的景观位。」→ I ended up at the counter, but it turned out to be the best view in the house.
「我没法准确描述伦敦是什么感觉。」→ I can't quite put my finger on what London is like.
「电影让这条街变成了全世界打卡的地方。」→ The movie put this street on the map for people all over the world.

ul.li: 「到了」别说 arrived to London → 地道说法是 made it to London 或 got to London。Arrive 后面用 in（大城市）/ at（小地点），不用 to。
「仪式感」不是 ceremony feeling → 用 ritual 或整体表达 get the ritual out of the way / check that box。
「下雨天不打伞」不是 in rainy days not use umbrella → 用 not bothering with umbrellas 或者 don't even bother with umbrellas，bother 表示「费那个劲」。
「账单也一样」不是 the bill is also the same → 语境是说账单跟体验一样令人印象深刻，说 the bill was just as impressive 或 the bill matched the view。
「看不出来特别之处」不是 can't see its special point → 说 can't tell what makes it special 或 don't see what the fuss is about。

div.p: 以前在旅行场景里只会说 I want to go to… 和 it's beautiful。现在看完这期视频，可以说：

ul.li: 「到了」→ We made it! 或 We've arrived!
「一定要做的游客打卡」→ the obligatory tourist stuff
「结果却是…」→ it turned out to be… / who would've thought…
「说不清楚」→ I can't quite put my finger on it
「让某个地方出名」→ put this place on the map
「价格很贵」→ pretty steep / works out to over…
「晴天终于来了」→ the sun finally came out
